purpose: Close a centered base-by-base pre-suppression air allocation and hardening model before re-running Nauru/Marshall/Tarawa suppression. Does not yet supersede GALVANIC v004 outcomes.
precedence_guards: No post-GALVANIC/FLINTLOCK defensive doctrine imported before 24 Nov 1943.
No 1944 Kinsei/aircraft maturity back-port; shore Kinsei detachment centered zero.
No historical Operation-RO 12-Nov Marshall drain unless a Branch-equivalent transfer is proven.
Aircraft existence, local allocation, serviceable and immediate sortie-ready are separate.
Kyofu/Zuiun are separate physical aircraft classes here and are not also hidden inside land-fighter/recon counts.
Hardening changes ground-loss coupling and repair persistence; it is not an air-combat multiplier.

regional_totals_center.note: Centers intentionally sit inside the pre-existing v048 bands: land fighters 80-95 physical, attack 35-45, legacy recon/water 15-20, Kyofu 12-20, Zuiun 5-9. Exact unit names remain partially unresolved.

fighter_type_guard.Raiden: centered physical 12 / serviceable 10, all within Taroa land-fighter slots as a priority-base interceptor detachment; no second shore Raiden unit credited before further trace
fighter_type_guard.Kinsei_Zero: 0 centered shore-combat allocation; scarce event-ready pool remains carrier-priority

attack_type_family_center.G4M_G3M_land_attack: roughly 18-22 physical across Taroa/Wotje/Kwaj/Nauru/Tarawa/Jaluit family; night/torpedo-qualified fraction separately constrained
attack_type_family_center.D4Y_D3A: roughly 10-14 physical, Mili-heavy with small Taroa/other detachments
attack_type_family_center.B6N: roughly 5-8 physical in the network, not a mass shore force; use only where local tools/spares/crew trace permits
attack_type_family_center.rule: The 11/23 ~22-aircraft torpedo strike must be regenerated from actual serviceable/night-qualified aircraft; do not simply consume all 30 serviceable attack aircraft.

bases.type_note: late-Zuisei fighter majority; no centered Raiden/Kinsei. Direct invasion warning encourages dispersion/evacuation of nonessential aircraft once the threat becomes legible.

hardening.aircraft_revetments: P2 dominant: coral/earth/log open-top dispersal pens; some more completely finished than historical
hardening.personnel_ammo: S1-S2 mix; historically reinforced-concrete/coconut-log bombproof shelters and magazines existed; Branch improves completion/dispersion rather than creating underground aircraft hangars

protection_assessment.direct_500lb_plus: LOW for aircraft pens; key S2 shelters much better for people/stores
protection_assessment.repeated_carrier_naval_saturation: LOW_TO_MODERATE due tiny island and known geometry

bases.operational_effect: Fewer cluster/chain ground losses and better survival of crews/ammo/comms; runway and aircraft still suppressible by repeated attack. Main GALVANIC effect is surviving beach-fire/C2 and some aircraft/crew preservation, not an unsuppressible air base.

hardening.aircraft_revetments: P2/P3 mix; historically extensive aircraft dispersal/revetments, fuel, workshops and multiple runways; some Marshall airbases used concreted revetments
hardening.support: multiple power/workshop/ammunition/fuel/C2 nodes; Branch adds dispersal, blast separation and plant uptime
hardening.branch_completion_delta: protected base works +10-25%; concrete-heavy roughly +5-15% where material/time allow

protection_assessment.geometry_ceiling: HIGH: flat, finite island remains mappable and repeat-strikeable

bases.operational_effect: The most important hardened Marshall air node. Same US sortie plan destroys fewer aircraft/support functions in one cycle; repeat strikes are still capable of systematic suppression.

bases.type_note: attack-heavy node, using historical Mili dive-bomber role as placement anchor while Branch allows a more mature D4Y/B6N fraction without replacing every legacy type.

hardening.aircraft_revetments: P2/P3 dispersal pens around major airfield; stores/C2/AA positions separately dispersed

bases.operational_effect: Attack aircraft are less likely to be destroyed in one ground sweep, but Mili can still be neutralized by sustained carrier/land-based suppression.

hardening.aircraft_revetments: P2/P3; historical airfield/seaplane infrastructure and concrete military revetments provide real lateral blast separation

bases.operational_effect: Hard target by 1943 atoll standards, but still an open-air base rather than a bombproof aircraft fortress.

hardening.runway: limited compared with main fighter nodes
hardening.water_air: ramp/fuel/radio/maintenance/support craft are separate targets; lagoon permits physical dispersal but not concealment from sustained search

protection_assessment.aircraft_afloat: LOW if visually located and strafed/bombed
protection_assessment.runway_independence: HIGHER than land-only bases because Kyofu/float search can persist after runway damage

bases.operational_effect: A suppression nuisance: US must attack ramp/fuel/support craft/communications separately. Hardening helps persistence more than individual-aircraft survivability.

hardening.airfield_base: P2/P3 revetments, command/logistics/submarine support and lagoon water-air facilities treated as multiple systems

bases.operational_effect: Hardening mainly protects command/logistics/search continuity. It does not imply the later Kwajalein landing beaches are already correctly oriented or deeply fortified.

hardening.natural_shelter: N1: raised terrain/excavations can protect personnel, small stores, repair/communications better than an atoll

protection_assessment.support_personnel_stores: MODERATE_TO_HIGH if moved into natural/engineered shelter

bases.operational_effect: Wasp/Princeton can still heavily suppress the node, but one strike day should not equal physical sterilization. Emergency recon/night staging can return after repair if follow-up pressure relaxes.

bases.center_rule: No resident combat-aircraft credit at T00 without a dated trace; seaplane/base infrastructure remains a target and can support transient aircraft before final alert evacuation.

hardening.manpower_cap: trained combat manpower remains dominant limit

bases.center_rule: Distributed, not a fictional single air group. Provides local cover/recon/staging only.

suppression_model_changes.aircraft_revetment_rule: Open-top revetments primarily prevent fragment/blast chain losses between dispersed aircraft; they do not make aircraft immune to direct bombs or effective strafing.
suppression_model_changes.runway_rule: Hardening does little to prevent crater creation. Branch advantage appears in rapid assessment, plant uptime, fill/repair, parallel taxi/dispersal use and keeping fuel/comms/maintenance from dying with the runway.
suppression_model_changes.same_plan_expected_direction: At equal US sortie count, fewer Japanese aircraft/support assets are destroyed on the ground and more bases require a repeat cycle. The effect is moderate, not immunity.
suppression_model_changes.no_flat_percentage: Exact ground-loss deltas must be generated target-by-target in the Nauru/Marshall suppression rerun.

reopen_implications: Nauru 11/23 remains heavily suppressed but residual support/repair survives more often.
Mili/Taroa/Wotje/Jaluit suppression consumes more target-identification/repeat-strike work.
Tarawa prelanding fire/C2/ammo/tank survival moves upward within existing OOB bands, especially if protected revetments and bombproof shelters survive.

If ground resistance or regional air persistence materially changes US CVE/fast-carrier deck state by 11/25-26, carrier battle mission-state must reopen; nominal carrier OOB alone cannot be held fixed.
